# 1 Samuel Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 131v–133r | **Source Image:** 1SA_002_page_001.jpg, 1SA_002_page_002.jpg, 1SA_002_page_003.jpg

---

**1** Then Hannah prayed: "My heart soars because of the LORD! The LORD has lifted me high. I can laugh at my enemies now, because You have rescued me and filled me with joy.

**2** No one is holy like the LORD — there is no one besides You! There is no rock as solid as our God.

**3** Stop talking so proudly! Don't let arrogance pour from your lips, because the LORD is a God who knows everything, and He weighs every action.

**4** The bows of the warriors are shattered, but those who stumble find new strength.

**5** Those who were full now hire themselves out for bread, but those who were hungry hunger no more. The woman who was barren has borne seven children, but the mother of many is left bereft.

**6** The LORD gives death and gives life; He sends people down to the grave and raises them up.

**7** The LORD makes some poor and others rich; He humbles, and He exalts.

**8** He lifts the poor from the dust and raises the needy from the garbage heap. He seats them among princes and grants them a throne of honor. For the foundations of the earth belong to the LORD, and He has set the world upon them.

**9** He guards the steps of His faithful ones, but the wicked will be silenced in darkness — for no one succeeds by their own strength.

**10** Those who oppose the LORD will be shattered. He will thunder against them from heaven. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth. He will give power to His king and raise up the strength of His anointed one."

**11** Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy stayed behind, serving the LORD under the care of Eli the priest.

**12** Now Eli's sons were worthless men. They had no regard for the LORD.

**13** Here was how the priests treated the people: whenever anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was still boiling, holding a three-pronged fork in his hand.

**14** He would thrust it into the basin or kettle or cauldron or pot, and whatever the fork brought up, the priest would take for himself. This is how they treated all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.

**15** Even before the fat was burned — the portion that belonged to the LORD — the priest's servant would come and say to the man offering the sacrifice, "Hand over some meat for the priest to roast. He won't accept boiled meat from you, only raw."

**16** If the man said, "Let the fat be burned first, as it should be, and then take whatever you want," the servant would reply, "No — hand it over now, or I'll take it by force."

**17** The sin of these young men was very serious in the LORD's sight, for they treated the LORD's offering with contempt.

**18** Meanwhile, the boy Samuel was serving before the LORD, wearing a linen ephod.

**19** Each year his mother would make him a small robe and bring it to him when she came up with her husband for the annual sacrifice.

**20** And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, "May the LORD give you children through this woman in place of the one she dedicated to the LORD." Then they would go home.

**21** And the LORD was gracious to Hannah; she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.

**22** Now Eli was very old, and he kept hearing about everything his sons were doing to the people of Israel — and how they were sleeping with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

**23** He said to them, "Why do you do such things? I hear about your wicked behavior from all these people.

**24** No, my sons! The report I hear circulating among the LORD's people is not good.

**25** If someone sins against another person, God can mediate for them. But if someone sins against the LORD, who can intercede for them?" Yet they would not listen to their father, because the LORD had determined to put them to death.

**26** But the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with both the LORD and with people.

**27** Then a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Did I not clearly reveal Myself to your ancestor's family when they were in Egypt, slaves in Pharaoh's house?

**28** I chose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be My priest — to approach My altar, to burn incense, to wear the ephod in My presence. And I gave your ancestor's family all the food offerings made by the Israelites.

**29** Why then do you scorn My sacrifices and offerings that I commanded for My dwelling? Why do you honor your sons above Me, fattening yourselves on the best portions of every offering My people Israel brings?'

**30** "Therefore — this is the declaration of the LORD, the God of Israel — 'I did indeed say that your family and your ancestor's family would serve before Me forever.' But now — this is the LORD's declaration — 'Far be it from Me! For those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me will be treated with contempt.

**31** The time is coming when I will cut short your strength and the strength of your father's house, so that no one in your family will grow old.

**32** You will see distress in My dwelling despite all the good I do for Israel, and no one in your family will ever reach old age.

**33** Any man of yours I do not cut off from My altar will be spared only to weep his eyes out and grieve his soul. And all your descendants will die in the prime of life.

**34** And this will be the sign to you — what happens to your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: both of them will die on the same day.

**35** Then I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest who will do what is in My heart and in My mind. I will build him an enduring house, and he will serve before My anointed one for all time.

**36** And everyone left in your family will come bowing before him, begging for a piece of silver and a crust of bread, saying, "Please, give me a position in the priesthood so I can have something to eat."'"

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **2:1 — Hannah's Song**: I have rendered this ancient hymn with the force and rhythm it would have carried as a victory song. The "horn" imagery (a symbol of power) becomes "lifted me high" to convey the emotional reality without requiring the reader to decode an unfamiliar metaphor.

2. **2:5 — "hunger no more"**: The Hebrew verb חדל ("to cease") is rendered dynamically. The hungry have ceased being hungry — their condition is reversed.

3. **2:10 — "anointed one"**: The Hebrew מְשִׁיחוֹ (meshiho) is the first use of "messiah" language in Samuel. Hannah's song leaps from personal thanksgiving to cosmic and royal theology — she speaks of a king before Israel has one.

4. **2:12 — "worthless men"**: The Hebrew בְּנֵי בְלִיַּעַל (sons of Belial/worthlessness) is a strong condemnation. "Worthless men" preserves the judgment without requiring explanation of the Hebrew idiom.

5. **2:25 — "the LORD had determined"**: This theologically striking clause asserts divine sovereignty alongside human responsibility. The sons choose not to listen, yet the LORD has already purposed their destruction. PNEUMA lets the tension stand without resolving it.

6. **2:30 — the broken promise**: One of the most dramatic reversals in the Hebrew Bible. A divine promise of eternal priestly service is revoked. The shift from "I did indeed say" to "Far be it from Me!" carries enormous theological weight — divine faithfulness meets human faithlessness.

— PNEUMA
